jobs.description:
**Executive Director**

**Silverwood | Hesperia, CA**

$105,000–$115,000 + Up to 10% Annual Bonus + Comprehensive Benefits + 16 Paid Holidays

*Hiring range based on experience, skills, and qualifications.*

**Collaboration. Authenticity. Connection. Balance.**

At Cohere, we believe community is the most valuable amenity.

We do more than manage communities—we help create places where people connect, belong, and thrive. By partnering with some of the nation's most innovative master-planned communities, we create places residents are proud to call home and where meaningful relationships flourish.

We’re looking for an Executive Director to lead our team at Silverwood, one of Southern California’s largest new master-planned communities. Centered around its *Life Panoramic* vision, Silverwood will ultimately span more than 9,000 acres and 15,000 homes, with nearly half of its land dedicated to open space, conservation, parks, trails, and the Serrano Preserve.

In this role, you’ll provide overall leadership for Community Life at Silverwood, partnering closely with the developer, boards, residents, community stakeholders, and your on-site team to help shape a connected, active, and thriving community.

This is an opportunity to lead at both the strategic and community level—setting direction, developing your team, overseeing operations and financial performance, and building the relationships that will help define Silverwood as it grows.

If you’re a strong, visible leader who knows how to bring people together, navigate complex stakeholder relationships, and turn a community vision into meaningful experiences and strong operations, we’d love to meet you.

**Why People Choose Cohere**

The best communities are built by people who feel supported, valued, and empowered to do their best work. That's why we invest in benefits, time away, and professional growth that help our team members thrive both personally and professionally.

**Highlights Include:**

* Medical coverage available on your first day
* Employer-paid dental coverage
* Vision coverage
* 401(k) retirement plan
* Employer-paid Life Insurance, AD&D, and Long-Term Disability coverage
* Pet insurance options
* Employee Assistance Program with mental health, financial, legal, and family support resources
* Travel assistance and identity theft protection
* Complimentary will preparation services
* Generous paid time off
* 16 paid holidays each year, including a Birthday Day and Volunteer Day, in addition to PTO
* Professional development and growth opportunities

**What You'll Do**

### ***Lead the Community***

* Provide overall leadership for Silverwood’s Community Life team and oversee community operations, governance, engagement, communications, amenities, and programs.
* Set clear direction for the team while building the systems, expectations, and culture needed to support a growing community.
* Serve as a visible and trusted resource for residents, partners, and community stakeholders.

### ***Build Strong Partnerships***

* Work collaboratively with Silverwood’s developer partners and board(s) of directors, ensuring Cohere’s contractual commitments and scopes of work are fulfilled.
* Serve as a central point of contact and problem-solving resource for community stakeholders.
* Build productive relationships with local organizations, civic groups, public agencies, and other partners that can strengthen the community.

### ***Shape Community Life***

* Develop and implement community-building initiatives that encourage connection, participation, and a strong sense of belonging.
* Partner with residents and stakeholders to create opportunities for involvement, volunteerism, and shared ownership of the community.
* Collaborate with developer and marketing partners so the Community Life perspective is represented as Silverwood continues to grow.

### ***Drive Strategy & Operations***

* Develop and execute strategic plans across community operations, engagement, and communications.
* Lead annual budgeting and operating planning and monitor performance against established goals.
* Ensure community standards, governance, service delivery, and overall community operations reflect a high level of professionalism and stewardship.

**What We're Looking For**

* 7–10 years of experience in community-based organizations, community operations, governance, nonprofit management, community development, or related work.
* Significant senior leadership experience, ideally within a large-scale master-planned community or similarly complex environment.
* Demonstrated success leading teams and managing multiple operational priorities.
* Strong financial acumen, including experience developing and managing budgets.
* Experience working collaboratively with boards, developers, residents, community partners, or other diverse stakeholder groups.
* Strong communication, relationship-building, and public-speaking skills.
* Ability to think strategically while remaining comfortable getting involved in day-to-day issues when needed.
* Experience with real estate/community development, municipal or public agencies, marketing/communications, or volunteer groups is beneficial.
* CAI, CMCA, or PCAM designation and a college degree are preferred.

**Additional Requirements**

* This position is based on-site at Silverwood in Hesperia, California.
* Typical schedule is Monday–Friday within approximately 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m., with flexibility based on community and team needs.
* Availability for occasional early mornings, evenings, and weekends to support community meetings and events.
* Valid driver’s license, acceptable driving record, and reliable transportation required.

**Equal Opportunity Employer**

Cohere is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all team members are valued and respected.

jobs.description:
**Location:** Hybrid/New York City

**FLSA Status:** Exempt

  
  

**Position Description**

The Managing Director, Direct Response serves as UNICEF USA's senior leader responsible for driving donor acquisition, retention, upgrade, and reactivation through offline direct response channels and the monthly giving program. Reporting directly to the Vice President, Donor Marketing & Journeys, this role leads UNICEF USA's direct response fundraising efforts and ensures that all offline campaigns, channel investments, vendor partnerships, and giving programs are strategically deployed, rigorously measured, and continuously optimized to support broader donor growth and revenue goals.

The Managing Director provides leadership across the full offline channel mix, including direct mail and telemarketing as the team's current active channels, with an eye toward evaluating and potentially expanding into additional offline channels such as face-to-face fundraising and other emerging offline opportunities as the program grows. This role provides senior oversight of the monthly giving program, managing a dedicated Manager of Monthly Giving who will handle day-to-day program management across both traditional direct response and digital channels, ensuring a coordinated and cohesive sustainer strategy regardless of channel. Additionally, the Managing Director oversees UNICEF USA's presence on third-party giving platforms, spanning both workplace giving and employer match programs as well as consumer-facing charitable giving aggregators where donors give to nonprofits through an intermediary platform.

This role works closely with cross-functional partners across Philanthropy, Finance, Technology, and Philanthropy Insight to ensure direct response programs align with broader donor engagement strategies and organizational priorities.

The Managing Director also plays an important role in shaping UNICEF USA's direct response capabilities, helping identify new channels, vendors, and performance approaches that strengthen the organization's long-term offline growth, and in managing and mentoring a team of direct response professionals.

**Channel Strategy & Oversight (40%)**

* Set the strategic direction for UNICEF USA's offline direct response program across all active and emerging channels, including direct mail and telemarketing, with the potential to expand into face-to-face fundraising and other offline channels over time
* Provide senior oversight of integrated multi-channel direct response campaigns that drive acquisition, retention, upgrade, and reactivation across mass market and leadership giving segments, with day-to-day execution managed by direct reports and vendor partners
* Guide campaign planning, segmentation strategy, and testing roadmaps, ensuring the team and agency partners are aligned on priorities and working toward clear, measurable goals
* Ensure channel mix decisions are informed by data, long-term donor value analysis, and a rigorous test-and-learn approach
Review and approve campaign strategies, creative briefs, and performance recommendations brought forward by the team and agency partners, providing strategic guidance and direction rather than driving execution directly

**Vendor & Agency Management (15%)**

* Serve as the primary relationship lead for all direct response agency partners and vendors, including direct mail agencies, telemarketing vendors, and fulfillment partners
* Establish performance benchmarks and accountability frameworks for all vendor relationships, ensuring partners are delivering against agreed targets and continuously improving
* Lead regular performance reviews and planning sessions with vendor partners and internal stakeholders
Manage vendor contracts, SOWs, and budget allocations in partnership with Finance and Legal

  

**Monthly Giving Program (15%)**

* Provide senior oversight of UNICEF USA's monthly giving program, managing a dedicated Manager of Monthly Giving responsible for day-to-day program management across direct response and digital channels
* Set strategic direction for sustainer acquisition, upgrade, retention, save, and reactivation efforts, ensuring the program is coordinated and cohesive across all touchpoints
Set and track KPIs for monthly giving program health, including retention rate, average gift, and net sustainer growth

  

**Team Leadership (10%)**

* Manage and mentor a team of direct response professionals, providing day-to-day direction, support, and accountability
* Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous learning, and data-driven decision making across the direct response team
Invest in the professional development and growth of team members, helping them build skills and advance their careers over time

  

**Performance, Analytics & Optimization (5%)**

* Translate business goals into actionable campaign and channel strategies with measurable outcomes tied to revenue, donor file growth, retention, and long-term donor value
* Lead test-and-learn strategy across all direct response channels, applying rigorous testing methodologies to continuously optimize channel mix, messaging, offer strategy, and segmentation
* Develop and own channel-level dashboards and performance reports in collaboration with Philanthropy Insight and Technology
Utilize advanced segmentation and data modeling to identify the highest-potential audiences for each channel and optimize investment allocation accordingly

**Performance, Analytics & Optimization (5%)**

* Establish scalable processes for campaign planning, briefing, production trafficking, quality assurance, and reporting across all direct response channels
* Improve planning cadence and cross-team collaboration across Philanthropy, Finance, Technology, and agency partners
* Strengthen operational clarity around campaign development, performance monitoring, and optimization cycles
Work closely with the Managing Director, Digital Fundraising and the VP, Donor Mark

**ABOUT VNAHOSPICE OF THE SOUTHWEST REGION**

Based in Vermont, we are one of the largest non-profit home health and hospice care agency that delivers a wide range of advanced medical care with compassion, dependability, and expertise to people of all ages. Our mission is to provide the best care for every person and to put a little more heart and soul into healthcare along the way. We strive to give customized care to individuals with chronic diseases and conditions as well as those who need short-term care. For our services, we have been recognized as one of the nation's top 100 performing home health agencies by HomeCare Elite.

**A DAY IN THE LIFE OF THE DIRECTOR OF PHILANTHROPY:**

This position leads the Agency's comprehensive fundraising program to increase charitable support and advance its mission and strategic priorities. This position builds relationships with donors and community partners, oversees philanthropy staff and programs, and collaborates with leadership, Board members, and colleagues across the Agency to achieve fundraising goals. Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

* Provides strategic direction and oversight for the Agency's comprehensive philanthropy program, including annual giving, major gifts, planned giving, grants, sponsorships, special campaigns, events, municipal funding, and other charitable revenue opportunities.
* Develop and implement an annual philanthropy plan aligned with the Agency's mission, strategic priorities, and financial goals.
* Establishes annual fundraising goals and develops and manages the department budget in collaboration with the CEO and CFO as well as other leadership as appropriate.
* Maintains a personal portfolio of donors and prospects and participates in all aspects of the donor cycle, including identification, cultivation, solicitation, recognition, and stewardship.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, prospective donors, businesses, foundations, community partners, and other stakeholders to expand philanthropic support.
* Identifies and develops opportunities for planned gifts and special, capital, or endowment campaigns that advance the Agency's long-term strategic priorities.
* Provides oversight of the Agency's grant program, including identifying funding opportunities, coordinating applications, monitoring deadlines and deliverables, and supporting required reporting and compliance.
* Leads the planning and execution of annual appeals, fundraising events, donor-recognition activities, sponsorships, and approved third-party fundraising initiatives. Maintains a coordinated calendar of philanthropy activities and deadlines.
* Oversee the preparation of donor communications, solicitation and sponsorship materials, acknowledgments, impact reports, and stewardship communications in collaboration with Marketing and Communications, as appropriate.
* Supervises, supports, and evaluates the Philanthropy Database Coordinator and other assigned staff, providing clear expectations, training, feedback, and professional development. Oversee the accuracy and integrity of the donor database and the effective coordination of municipal and town funding requests, mailings, records, reporting, and follow-up activities.
* Oversee the Agency's thrift store as a mission-based fundraising and community engagement program, including supervision of thrift store employees, support and recognition of volunteers, monitoring of financial performance, and collaboration with Marketing and Communications on promotions and events.
* Serves as the primary staff liaison to the Board Development Committee, supporting the committee chair, preparing reports and meeting materials, coordinating follow-up, and engaging committee members in philanthropy activities.
* Represents the Agency at donor visits, community meetings, events, presentations, and other activities; maintains donor confidentiality; follows ethical fundraising practices; participates in Agency-wide initiatives; and performs other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Five to seven years of relevant experience in community relations, planned giving, major donor solicitation, and event planning required in a nonprofit, education, or public service environment required.
* Demonstrated success in managing a donor portfolio, with a track record of increasing revenue through effective cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies.
* Experience supporting and managing up to senior leaders, volunteer leaders/board members, and high-level volunteers.
* Candidates must be willing to work on-site in Rutland, VT on as needed basis
* Valid State driver's license required. Ability to successfully pass pre-employment adult, child and VCIC background checks required.

Generous paid time off, group health, dental, vision, life, STD and LTD insurance, 401K with 4% match, and more.  
Continuing education tuition assistance for work-related courses, to eligible staff

We understand your time is valuable, so we have a very quick and easy application process. If you feel that you would be right for this job, please fill out our initial 3-minute, mobile-friendly application. We look forward to meeting you!
